thread:
Sara: heads-up, I'm seeing an uptick of CUDA faults and container OOMs in eu-west cluster. Started ~2025-11-02T09:12Z, node worker-gpu-11.
Ops-bot: Incident logged: INC-20251102-0912 severity=high. Assigned: @oncall-gpu. Paging schedule activated.
Kevin: can you paste the tail of the logs from worker-gpu-11? need Xid/code and container exits
Sara: paste from node:
```
[2025-11-02T09:11:46Z] runtime: illegal memory access at 0x7ffd80000000
[09:11:46] service: kv_cache::batch_read+0x1f7
[09:11:46] containerd: container runtime exited (status 137)
[09:11:46] kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID=17645, GPU fault
[09:11:47] runtime: segmentation violation during cudaMemcpy
```
Dmitri: I'm oncall. Cordoning node now and evicting pods.
Dmitri: `kubectl cordon worker-gpu-11` then `kubectl drain worker-gpu-11 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=40`
Infra-bot: worker-gpu-11 cordoned. Evicting 9 pods. Reason: suspected GPU pagewalk/device fault.
Maria: routing team — flipping eu region traffic to cpu-fallback model variant (small-quant-cpu) for affected routes. Applying route override for 15min.
Ben: customer impact tracking: saw elevated 500s for two customers (DataCorps, MetricsHub) and three internal evaluation jobs. Peak error rate ~4.8% in eu for last 10m.
Kevin: Xid 79 again; suspects either device ECC/firmware or a kernel-level pagewalk race. Also note repeated oom-kills (exit 137) which suggests memory pressure preceding fault.
Sara: I'm disabling shared KV prefix cache on the runtime for the affected service to reduce concurrent mmap/read paths that might trigger the crash.
Sara: runtime config applied:
```
service.runtime.cache.prefix_kv.enabled=false
service.runtime.retries=2
service.runtime.batch.max_tokens=6
```
Dmitri: initiating hotfix build with extra pointer safety checks in native JNI layer. Will canary to non-prod first.
Ops-bot: Deploy started: runtime-hotfix-20251102-canary -> cluster: canary-eu (3 pods)
Infra-bot: collecting GPU diagnostics: `nvidia-smi -q` and nvlog archive. Noted corrected ECC counters increment before fault on worker-gpu-11.
Sara: NV logs show correctable ECC spikes preceding the Xid. Opening cloud provider ticket for hardware swap on worker-gpu-11.
Maria: statuspage update posted: "Investigating GPU runtime errors in EU-West. Some requests may fall back to CPU models or see 5xx. Mitigations in progress."
Ben: mitigation metrics: after route override + cache bypass, 5xx rate down from 4.8% -> 0.9%. Customers rerouted: DataCorps, MetricsHub. No evidence of data leakage.
Kevin: if canary hotfix is stable for 12 minutes, we'll promote. If not, roll back to previous runtime and keep CPU fallback.
Dmitri: after cordon I saw a similar Xid on worker-gpu-14 during pod reschedule. Cordoning gpu-14 too. Now suspect a software race under particular workload pattern not exclusive to single card.
Sara: repro hypothesis: concurrent KV cache reads with long contexts lead to stale pointer bridging between CPU mmaped pages and GPU-initiated DMA pagewalks -> misaligned access in kernel/driver under stress.
Ben: action items logged: 1) keep nodes cordoned until hardware diag, 2) keep CPU fallback for critical customers, 3) run targeted load tests to reproduce with eng-runtime+eng-ml.
Dmitri: handoff: I'll leave notes in the incident doc and hand over to @Oncall-GPU-Next at 10:30Z for verification and to authorize wider rollout.
Oncall-GPU-Next: acknowledged, I'll pick this up at 10:30Z. Will monitor Xid occurrences and confirm hotfix telemetry.
Kevin: timeline summary: detection 09:12 -> cordon 09:14 -> traffic fallback 09:16 -> cache bypass 09:18 -> canary deploy 09:24. Current status: canary running; error rate reduced; hardware ticket opened; further investigation pending.
Sara: collect kernel oops, runtime heap dumps, nvlog, and container coredumps for postmortem. Tossing flags to eng-runtime and eng-ml to reproduce with scaled KV workload.
Ben: customer comms follow-up: we'll post an update within 30m summarizing impact, mitigations, and next steps including potential hardware replacement if provider confirms faulty ECC behavior.
Ops-bot: Reminder: next on-call takeover in 1 hour -> paging @Oncall-GPU-Next. Incident channel will remain active until resolved.
Kevin: thanks all. keep this thread as single source for updates. ping me for any new Xid 79 or OOM 137 events.
Oncall-GPU-Next: will report back after verification sweep and telemetry checks.
